findings.title: Non-consuming terminators are deleted by an expansion
findings.reproduction: Configure non-auto teh -> the and type teh followed by Space. ergopti_hotstrings.lua:594-598 passes is_terminator as terminator_consumed; the engine requests four backspaces and the injector writes only the, leaving no Space.
findings.root_cause: The Linux boundary substitutes terminator presence for the catalogue's consume policy and does not carry a terminator replay operation.
findings.silent_failure: The injector is not given the terminator identity or policy, so it reports a normal successful expansion.
findings.regression_test: Assert exact final uinput text for Space, comma, period, Enter, Tab, and a custom consume=true terminator through hook, daemon, engine, and injector.

findings.title: Enter and Tab never reach the matcher as terminators
findings.reproduction: Type a non-auto trigger followed by Enter or Tab. keyboard_hook.lua:274-277 dispatches only a control event and daemon on_control resets the engine without calling engine:on_char.
findings.root_cause: Control-key routing has no domain event for textual terminators even though the shared catalogue declares Enter and Tab.
findings.silent_failure: The buffer reset is treated as normal control handling and produces no error.
findings.regression_test: Drive Enter and Tab from hook to engine and assert one expansion plus exact key replay.

findings.title: Captured text does not follow active XKB state
findings.reproduction: Run the standard service under XKB fr and press physical keycode 30: the desktop produces q while the Linux reader records a. CapsLock, AltGr, groups, and dual Shift state also diverge.
findings.root_cause: Capture uses static qwerty/azerty tables and role booleans instead of the live XKB keymap, keycode set, locks, and groups.
findings.silent_failure: Unknown real layout identifiers fall back to a valid-looking QWERTY path and only Ergopti's internal buffer is wrong.
findings.regression_test: Compare captured characters to an XKB oracle for us, fr, CapsLock, AltGr, dual Shift, dead/compose keys, multi-group, and hot group changes.

findings.title: Grabbed input pass-through and injection are not failure-atomic
findings.reproduction: Make the uinput backend return false for EV_KEY or SYN while EVIOCGRAB is held: the physical event is drained, callbacks continue, and undo/metrics can commit. Holding RightShift during an expansion can synthesize and leave LeftShift down; an exception after modifier-up skips restoration.
findings.root_cause: False emission results are ignored, modifier identity is collapsed to roles, cleanup is success-tail-only, and logical state has no output commit boundary.
findings.silent_failure: False does not fail pcall and completion logs/state updates continue without an observed output effect.
findings.regression_test: Fail every individual key/SYN emission and throw after modifier release; assert emergency ungrab, exact balanced modifier keycodes, no swallowed physical key, and no undo/metric commit.

findings.title: Dynamic hotstrings fire after any following character
findings.reproduction: Register suffix td with magic key ★ and invoke on_trigger with buffer tdx and trigger x; the manager injects the date result and returns true.
findings.root_cause: on_trigger substitutes the current character into t and checks only that the buffer ends with t, never that trigger equals the configured magic key.
findings.silent_failure: The tautological suffix check is documented as a magic-key guard and current tests do not use a wrong following character.
findings.regression_test: Assert tdx/x is false and td★/★ is true, including the daemon caller.

findings.title: Personal dynamic output reaches injection without privacy metadata
findings.reproduction: Expand a personal-info rule such as @i★ and inspect the injector call; dynamic_hotstrings/manager.lua:382-385 passes no third is_private argument.
findings.root_cause: Privacy is derived only for the event returned after injection rather than at the injection/logging boundary.
findings.silent_failure: The manager's own log is redacted while injector success or failure logs can still contain plaintext.
findings.regression_test: Use logger and injector spies for success and failure and assert that no personal payload appears and is_private is mandatory true.

findings.title: Enabling gestures after boot does not start the touchpad reader
findings.reproduction: Initialize gestures disabled, then call enable or use the menu toggle. is_enabled becomes true while the reader remains closed and pump returns zero.
findings.root_cause: enable only changes a boolean; only init with enabled=true invokes start_reading.
findings.silent_failure: The menu and state report enabled even though no device is read.
findings.regression_test: Initialize false, enable, assert fake reader open and action dispatch; inject open failure and assert enabled remains false with a visible error.

findings.title: Magic-key configuration accepts unsafe keys and leaves static mappings on the old key
findings.reproduction: MagicKey.validate('e') returns true. Changing ★ to § reloads the catalogue, but the loader copies literal triggers; 940 of 2,121 mappings still end in ★.
findings.root_cause: Validation uses a short blacklist rather than a shared safe-codepoint policy, and the catalogue loader has no configured magic-key substitution owner.
findings.silent_failure: The dialog persists the choice and the daemon logs re-registration although most static mappings still listen to the old key.
findings.regression_test: Reject letters/digits and ordinary word codepoints; accept safe symbols; after custom-key reload/restart assert every owned trigger uses the new key and none uses the old one.

findings.title: Dynamic-rule counters grow on repeated initialization
findings.reproduction: Call dynamic_hotstrings.init twice with the same data; get_rules_count changes from 3 to 6 although the engine contains three active rules.
findings.root_cause: Engine rules are reset but the module-level _rules_count is not reset before registration.
findings.silent_failure: Actual rules are replaced correctly, so only menu counts and logs drift.
findings.regression_test: Assert identical rule and active counts across repeated init, reload, and magic-key changes.

findings.title: A non-committed TOML parse replaces the last healthy source
findings.reproduction: Make Reader.parse return its current empty result with committed=false for one personal source while other packs remain valid; Linux loader captures only pcall ok,data and installs the aggregate without that source or a precise parse failure.
findings.root_cause: The Linux loader ignores the shared reader's committed return and has no per-source last-known-good staging transaction.
findings.silent_failure: Other valid packs keep the global mapping count nonzero and the invalid source quietly disappears.
findings.regression_test: Inject read, semantic, and close failures; retain the previous source snapshot, increment the exact error count, and swap only a fully committed aggregate.

findings.title: Persistence operations and callers can report success without a durable commit
findings.reproduction: Set XDG_CONFIG_HOME to /dev/null and call Storage.set: it reports true and reads from cache in-process, but a fresh module load cannot read the value. Dynamic rules, shortcuts, hotstring state, magic reset, updater, LLM, keylogger/WPM, and an editor path also discard Storage mutation results and publish state/success.
findings.root_cause: _flush can return false and does not check every I/O stage; set/delete/clear ignore its result and publish cache first, while multiple mutating consumers do not propagate the port result.
findings.silent_failure: The in-memory state and UI appear correct until restart even when no durable commit occurred.
findings.regression_test: Fault open, short write, close, rename, and corrupt JSON across every caller family; no mutator may publish success/state before commit, and reload must preserve recoverable prior data.

findings.title: An explicit input device is replaced by auto-detection
findings.reproduction: Start with --device /dev/input/event7 while auto-detection prefers event3 and run eight watchdog ticks; the hook switches to event3.
findings.root_cause: The hook stores the current path but not whether selection ownership is pinned or automatic.
findings.silent_failure: The switch is logged as ordinary hotplug behavior.
findings.regression_test: With fake event7 pinned and event3 preferred, retain/reacquire event7 across watchdog checks and same-path reconnect.

findings.title: Only one keyboard and one pointer are observed
findings.reproduction: Use a laptop keyboard plus USB keyboard without a working consolidated Kanata output; device_finder and keyboard_hook maintain only one scalar keyboard slot, so one device bypasses Ergopti. A healthy Kanata aggregate can mitigate this conditional case.
findings.root_cause: Device selection and hook state are single-device abstractions.
findings.silent_failure: The selected device works normally and there is no warning that other eligible devices are unobserved.
findings.regression_test: Exercise two simultaneous keyboards and multiple pointers through hotplug; assert both feed one ordered state or that a required consolidated device is explicitly health-checked.

findings.title: Pointer and keyboard queues can reverse real input order
findings.reproduction: Queue a pointer click at timestamp T and a key at T+1 before one pump. keyboard_hook drains the keyboard queue fully before the pointer queue, dispatching the key first.
findings.root_cause: Independent device queues are not merged by kernel timestamp.
findings.silent_failure: Each individual queue remains internally ordered, hiding the cross-device inversion.
findings.regression_test: Merge fixtures by timestamp with deterministic ties and assert both click-before-key and key-before-click cases preserve the real order and buffer reset boundary.

findings.title: Fatal evdev reads are treated as temporary empty reads
findings.reproduction: Return ENODEV/HUP or a short read, then reconnect a device at the same eventN. evdev_reader returns nil and keeps the fd; is_open remains true and the watchdog does not reacquire.
findings.root_cause: The reader collapses event, would-block, short/fatal read, and exceptions into data-or-nil and does not expose errno/revents.
findings.silent_failure: No lifecycle transition or fatal diagnostic occurs while the path and stored fd still look unchanged.
findings.regression_test: Return event/would_block/fatal explicitly; inject ENODEV, HUP, short read, and same-name reconnect and assert teardown plus reacquisition.

findings.title: Trigger timeout checks only the final inter-key interval
findings.reproduction: For trigger abcd with 750 ms delay, type a, wait one second, then type bcd quickly; the match can pass because only the interval immediately before the match is checked.
findings.root_cause: Delay is evaluated only after a match exists and uses one global last-key timestamp rather than timestamps aligned to the candidate buffer.
findings.silent_failure: The earlier pause is no longer observable when the matcher returns a result.
findings.regression_test: Insert an excessive pause at every position of a multi-character trigger and assert invalidation plus correct resets on click/control/focus.

findings.title: Modifier and CapsLock events bypass physical key metrics
findings.reproduction: Press only Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Meta, or CapsLock while observing onPhysical; keyboard_hook returns from modifier/lock branches before invoking the callback.
findings.root_cause: Physical event publication occurs after early interpretation branches instead of before them.
findings.silent_failure: Text input continues and the daemon comment claims all physical events are recorded, while heatmaps/holds omit them.
findings.regression_test: Assert exactly one physical down/up event for every modifier/lock without emitting a character.

findings.title: Kanata can be reported started after immediate process failure
findings.reproduction: Use a Kanata executable that exits code 1 immediately; platform/remap/manager.lua accepts the shell-printed background PID and returns success without readiness.
findings.root_cause: Startup ownership proves only that a PID was printed, not process stability, configuration acceptance, or output-device readiness.
findings.silent_failure: The short-lived PID is treated as an owned running daemon and stderr/readiness is not part of the result.
findings.regression_test: Require bounded owned-process and output-device readiness; an immediate exit or rejected config must return false with captured diagnostics.

findings.title: Module-load and event-pump failures are swallowed
findings.reproduction: Inject an exception into an enabled optional require or the keyboard/tray/gesture/lifecycle pump; multiple daemon pcall sites discard the error or degrade without a capability state.
findings.root_cause: Required and optional modules are not classified and protected callbacks lack a centralized error/lifecycle policy.
findings.silent_failure: An enabled feature can disappear, and a keyboard pump can stop while grab state remains, without a surfaced health error.
findings.regression_test: Inject require and pump exceptions; required load fails startup safely, optional load becomes visible unavailable, and keyboard pump failure tears down/ungrabs with traceback.

findings.title: Secure-field probe failures are treated as non-secure fields
findings.reproduction: Remove the accessibility D-Bus, make popen fail, or return malformed role data; secure_field_detector resolves nil and refresh publishes secure=false to keylogger consumers.
findings.root_cause: The adapter cannot distinguish insecure from unknown/probe failure and converts all nil outcomes to false.
findings.silent_failure: Privacy-sensitive consumers see an ordinary non-password field instead of degraded detection.
findings.regression_test: Expose secure/insecure/unknown and test missing bus, spawn error, malformed response, timeout, password role, and normal role with fail-closed privacy.

findings.title: Ollama endpoint composition produces invalid URLs
findings.reproduction: Resolve a normal Ollama profile: llm_bridge returns an endpoint ending /api/chat, profiles appends /api/tags, and api_ollama appends /api/chat, producing /api/chat/api/tags and /api/chat/api/chat.
findings.root_cause: A value named base_url mixes provider origin and operation endpoint; independent callers append operation paths again.
findings.silent_failure: Tests pin the malformed base or mock popen without checking the final URL.
findings.regression_test: Run profile-to-API integration against a fake HTTP server and assert exact /api/tags and /api/chat requests.

findings.title: Synchronous LLM transport blocks the grabbed keyboard loop
findings.reproduction: Point Ollama at a slow or hung server and type enough to request prediction; api_ollama uses blocking io.popen and drains the response in the keystroke call path, preventing keyboard pump and cancel input.
findings.root_cause: A synchronous subprocess is wrapped in callback-shaped APIs and called from the single event loop while EVIOCGRAB is active.
findings.silent_failure: Fast mocked commands return immediately and cancellation only marks state without terminating the process.
findings.regression_test: Use a slow/hung server; assert physical input continues, timeout is bounded, cancel kills the process group, one terminal callback fires, and stale completion cannot publish.

findings.title: LLM text delivery hides failure and deletes UTF-8 by byte count
findings.reproduction: Make ydotool/xdotool fail: TextSender ignores shell_run false and invokes its completion callback without an error result or log, so downstream state cannot distinguish delivery. Accept a prediction after typing é: prediction_engine uses #string and requests two deletions.
findings.root_cause: LLM delivery bypasses the owned injector contract, has no failure channel beyond a completion-only callback, and uses byte length instead of the shared character deletion metric.
findings.silent_failure: Prediction state and metrics can advance despite no delivered text or excess deletion.
findings.regression_test: Route through the transactional injector and test missing tool/command failure plus é, combining text, and emoji with exact final text and state commit.

findings.title: LLM settings have inconsistent persistence and default ownership
findings.reproduction: Toggle LLM from the tray and restart: prediction_engine.toggle only changes memory although enable/disable persist. URL filtering defaults true in manifest.toml but false in shared defaults and the Linux bridge.
findings.root_cause: The menu calls a noncanonical setter and the same default has multiple handwritten owners.
findings.silent_failure: The current session reflects the toggle, masking restart drift; each source appears locally valid.
findings.regression_test: Make toggle delegate to the persisted authority and generate the URL-filter default; assert restart and cross-driver projection parity.

findings.title: Updater asset selection expects the wrong name and falls back arbitrarily
findings.reproduction: Present the assets emitted by CI: updater expects ergopti_linux.tar.gz while CI publishes ergopti-plus-linux.tar.gz, then selects the first browser_download_url regardless of package kind.
findings.root_cause: CI and updater do not consume one artifact manifest and fallback is positional rather than platform/architecture/type exact.
findings.silent_failure: Any sufficiently large downloaded asset advances to extraction/install.
findings.regression_test: Shuffle tar/zip/deb/rpm/AppImage assets with similar names; require exactly the canonical platform/architecture artifact or a closed failure.

findings.title: Self-update staging moves its own source and replaces the wrong install root
findings.reproduction: Use the real release tar layout. Unnormalized install_dir .../linux/modules/updater/../.. makes backup .../linux/modules/...old inside its own source, so the first mv necessarily fails; staging is also inside that tree. Numeric nonzero LuaJIT shell status remains truthy, and a nominal replacement would nest linux/linux and leave _shared stale.
findings.root_cause: Updater fails to normalize/own the complete install root, constructs a backup inside its source, stages inside its move target, assumes the wrong archive root, and does not normalize process status or model install types.
findings.silent_failure: No complete-root layout/version/wrapper smoke is required before success and numeric exit semantics can invert checks.
findings.regression_test: Upgrade an actual N artifact to N+1 and verify wrapper, Linux, and _shared; fault every stage and assert atomic rollback for tar installs while package installs delegate.

findings.title: Updater transport is blocking and accepts unauthenticated content
findings.reproduction: Serve a slow response, an archive download returning a large HTML/error body, bad archive hash, or path traversal entry. Metadata GET checks an appended HTTP code, but archive download omits --fail, ignores pipe:close, and relies on size; Timer can silently drop scheduled checks without luv.
findings.root_cause: Archive transport, scheduler, integrity, extraction, and cancellation capabilities are fragmented and download success is inferred from stderr/size rather than exit/status/content trust.
findings.silent_failure: A large body or absent timer can look like a valid download or configured scheduled update without a trustworthy failure state.
findings.regression_test: Test slow/hung, 404 HTML, cancel, missing event loop, traversal, bad digest/signature, malformed manifest, and one terminal callback using bounded async transport.

findings.title: Standalone Kanata installation uses obsolete and cross-OS assets
findings.reproduction: Run standalone installation without preinstalled Kanata. x86_64 selects obsolete asset name kanata and ARM64 selects kanata_macos_arm64; on the audit date both latest URLs return 404. Download failure is converted to optional success, while any downloaded file only has to be generically executable, so a Mach-O ARM binary would pass and fail later under Linux.
findings.root_cause: A mutable latest URL, stale raw asset names, an OS-confused architecture map, and permission-only postconditions replace a pinned Linux artifact manifest and runtime validation.
findings.silent_failure: The installer continues and prints completion after download failure; standalone CI never checks Kanata/remap, and an accepted cross-OS file fails only when the service starts.
findings.regression_test: Fixture-test pinned Linux archives, 404, Mach-O, wrong-architecture ELF, checksum failure, and asset-name mutation; prove kanata --version plus remap readiness on supported architectures or an explicit unsupported ARM result.

findings.title: Distro dependency and package smoke coverage can pass without required capabilities
findings.reproduction: Run Alpine dependency selection: apk reuses a positional package column intended for another manager and may omit xkbcli. CI distro installs use root with --no-deps; PKGBUILD/Nix are not built and AppImage is only host-Ubuntu-smoked. The shipped PKGBUILD retains pkgver=__VERSION__, follows branch=dev, and uses SKIP checksums while its gate checks only payload/LUA_PATH.
findings.root_cause: Dependency ownership is positional across package managers and package verification checks layout/help rather than fresh-user runtime capability.
findings.silent_failure: Root checkout tools satisfy probes and --no-deps bypasses the package contract while jobs remain green.
findings.regression_test: Use manager-specific tables with postcondition probes; perform fresh native installs and build PKGBUILD/Nix on supported architectures plus AppImage old-glibc/unsupported-musl cases.

findings.title: Packages claim service readiness while suppressing enablement and permission failures
findings.reproduction: Install deb/rpm where systemctl --user cannot reach the target user's bus; scripts mask failure with || true and print enabled. Package smokes do not establish udev/groups/modules or normal-user input access.
findings.root_cause: Privilege/session setup is not one package-owned transaction and status messages are unconditional.
findings.silent_failure: The package install exits successfully and static --help/layout smoke passes although the daemon cannot capture or inject.
findings.regression_test: Fresh normal-user install, relogin/reboot, service start, real input capture/injection, tray/WebKit, upgrade/remove, and injected no-bus/permission failures with truthful guidance.

findings.title: The Linux action picker is unreachable and its catalogue is incomplete
findings.reproduction: Search production callers: none opens action_picker. Its bridge requires nonexistent Linux modules.gestures.actions and emits empty items. Shared actions.toml has 79 all-platform IDs; Linux labels 42, misses 39 user actions, adds three noncanonical IDs, and open_paths_editor opens the wrong page.
findings.root_cause: Linux hand-maintains a partial action namespace and the bridge was copied against a macOS-only module rather than generated from the shared source.
findings.silent_failure: The lazy WebView registration and pcall fallback make the feature appear present while assignment has no production path or items.
findings.regression_test: Enforce actions.toml-to-picker-to-executor bijection and E2E select, persist, restart, and trigger every supported action class including each open target.

findings.title: Six shared WebViews are dormant and protocol-incompatible
findings.reproduction: Replay shipped JS messages for download, model browser, paths editor, personal-info editor, prompt editor, and token prompt against Linux bridges; message types/fields disagree, some methods do not exist, prompt title is written as prompt, token actions are disjoint, and success can be returned without a writer. No production opener exists for five; the paths editor is also dormant.
findings.root_cause: Registration was treated as parity without a versioned shared host protocol, production caller, or real persistence owner.
findings.silent_failure: Lazy registration and permissive bridge success responses make source/test presence look functional.
findings.regression_test: Contract-test actual script.js messages and E2E open, initialize, modify, save, restart, read/apply; no success response without an observed committed effect.

findings.title: Shortcut master toggle neither gates configured bindings nor persists
findings.reproduction: Disable shortcuts from the menu, trigger a configured slot, then restart. CapsWord consults the toggle, but keyboard_shortcuts dispatch continues and manager state is memory-only.
findings.root_cause: There is no single persisted shortcut-enable authority at the common dispatch boundary.
findings.silent_failure: The menu checkmark changes while most bindings remain active and restart restores the boot default.
findings.regression_test: Off blocks slots, CapsWord, and all shortcut actions before dispatch; persist both states and assert restart behavior and failed-save rollback.

findings.title: Selection transformations are X11-only and fail silently on Wayland
findings.reproduction: Invoke a selection transform on a Wayland session without xclip/xdotool; shortcuts/manager.lua shells to those X11 tools, ignores failures, and can return without a visible effect. Non-ASCII case conversion is byte-limited.
findings.root_cause: Selection/clipboard/injection and Unicode transformation are embedded X11 shell operations instead of capability adapters.
findings.silent_failure: The exposed action remains enabled and important external command results are not surfaced.
findings.regression_test: Test X11 and GNOME/KDE/wlroots Wayland, missing tools, terminal paste, and non-ASCII text; require exact transformed output or an explicit disabled reason.

findings.title: Per-application configuration opens only generic configuration
findings.reproduction: Activate the Linux menu row declared as per-application configuration; menu_builder opens hotstrings_config_window with no application identity or profile context.
findings.root_cause: A shared menu promise is wired to a generic placeholder callback without an app-profile storage/application model.
findings.silent_failure: A valid configuration window opens, obscuring that no per-app transaction occurred.
findings.regression_test: Implement and test two app identities with different persisted/applied settings across focus and restart, or assert the row is absent/renamed until supported.

findings.title: Spotlight is absent despite an all-platform action declaration
findings.reproduction: Resolve spotlight_mouse from actions.toml, which declares platform=all; Windows and macOS have production implementations while Linux has no implementation or caller.
findings.root_cause: Canonical platform support was not reconciled with the Linux capability/executor projection.
findings.silent_failure: Structural/parity checks do not require a Linux production caller for every all-platform action.
findings.regression_test: Either exercise a compositor-safe Linux overlay across scale/multi-monitor or make the intentional Linux omission explicit in the canonical action and parity gate.

findings.title: The Linux unit runner succeeds with zero executed tests
findings.reproduction: Run lua5.4 tests/run.lua --only __NO_SUCH_TEST_CASE__; it reports zero modules, zero passed, zero failed and exits 0. Missing discovery support can also lead to empty success.
findings.root_cause: Runner discovery and selection have no checked module/test manifest or minimums, unmatched filters are not errors, and discovery completion is not fully validated.
findings.silent_failure: Zero failures is treated as success regardless of whether any assertion ran.
findings.regression_test: Self-test empty directory, missing dependency, unmatched filter, discovery error, and partial manifest; each must fail while a valid explicit subset proves a nonzero expected count.

findings.title: Pseudo-E2E passes without its corpus and ignores exact backspace expectations
findings.reproduction: Remove the corpus and run E2E: it warns and passes 9/9. Change a vector's expected.backspace_count to 999: it still passes 43/43 because the numeric oracle is reduced to a permissive boolean/alternative.
findings.root_cause: Corpus loading is optional and the Linux runner does not compare the exact platform expectation.
findings.silent_failure: Built-in smoke vectors and tolerant alternatives keep the headline suite green.
findings.regression_test: Make corpus/floors mandatory, assert exact platform values, and mutation-test every expected field so each semantic mutation fails.

findings.title: Mandatory-looking Linux CI subjects may be skipped while the aggregate remains green
findings.reproduction: Follow Wayland, WebKit, and LuaJIT-distro skip paths in ci.yml: missing status/socket/page prerequisites can exit 0. The linux-ok aggregate accepts skipped dependencies and rejects only failure/cancelled.
findings.root_cause: CI has no machine-owned mandatory coverage manifest and aggregate logic conflates skipped/not-run with successful assertion execution.
findings.silent_failure: The aggregate checkmark is green despite absent subject evidence.
findings.regression_test: Feed the aggregate every result state and require success plus an assertion artifact for every mandatory subject; skipped/missing mandatory entries must fail.

findings.title: Linux parity state is not governed by current manifests and gates
findings.reproduction: Generate the Linux feature manifest: 126 entries are supported and 198 unavailable, with 194 unavailable entries lacking a reason key. Run test:manifest-parity: it compares only AHK and Hammerspoon. Existing reachability does not distinguish registration, production caller, persistence, application, or hardware proof.
findings.root_cause: Linux is not a first-class projection of the canonical parity model and capability proof tiers are absent.
findings.silent_failure: Presence/reference counts and a Windows/macOS-only green command are read as Linux parity evidence.
findings.regression_test: Generate Linux status/reason/owner/caller/persisted/applied/proof-tier data, validate exposed unavailable reasons, include it in parity gates, and enforce bidirectional fake conformance.

findings.title: Stale status, skip ownership, and hardcoded user text obscure Linux reality
findings.reproduction: Compare todo_linux.md and Linux READMEs with production callers: notifier, gesture reader, shortcuts, crypto, and LLM are described as absent despite current code. Four conformance skips point to nonexistent Lot5 Linux parity ownership, and several Linux user-facing strings are hardcoded French.
findings.root_cause: Status prose, skip debt, and localization are manually maintained outside the canonical capability/i18n sources.
findings.silent_failure: Developers and users receive contradictory state while existing path/locale gates do not cover these claims.
findings.regression_test: Generate/link capability status, require every skip owner path/ID and expiry, route user strings through i18n, and gate doc links plus locale completeness.

findings.title: Keyboard capture ignores SYN_DROPPED and never resynchronizes
findings.reproduction: Feed keyboard_hook SYN_DROPPED, a release event that is lost during overflow, SYN_REPORT, then a normal key. keyboard_hook.lua:228 discards every EV_SYN and no keyboard code calls EVIOCGKEY, so stale modifier and text state continue.
findings.root_cause: The keyboard path treats synchronization events as irrelevant instead of entering the Linux input recovery protocol: ignore until SYN_REPORT, query EVIOCG state, then resume from a rebuilt snapshot.
findings.silent_failure: Overflow is discarded as an ordinary synchronization event; blocking work can make overflow more likely while stale state remains plausible.
findings.regression_test: Inject a synthetic overflow with a lost Shift release; require interpretation pause, exact EVIOCG resynchronization, candidate-buffer invalidation, and fail-safe teardown when resync fails.

findings.title: Gesture assignments commit in memory when TOML persistence fails
findings.reproduction: Initialize production gestures with persist=true, inject TomlWriter.batch_write returning false, and set a binding or parameter. manager.lua mutates memory first, ignores _persist_updates, reports/rebuilds the new state, and restart loses it; reset-all and disable-all have the same shape.
findings.root_cause: Gesture configuration has no stage-write-publish transaction and public mutators discard the exact persistence result.
findings.silent_failure: The menu is rebuilt from changed memory and matches the user's choice until restart.
findings.regression_test: Fault open/write/close/rename for one binding, one parameter, reset-all, and disable-all; require false propagation, unchanged prior state, and identical restart state.

findings.title: Tooltip category resolution fails open
findings.reproduction: Provide tooltip preview a category resolver that throws or returns a malformed value for a category whose committed policy is show_tooltip=false; preview.lua:207-215 returns true and Renderer.show is called.
findings.root_cause: Missing or failed configuration resolution is converted to the permissive display default instead of retaining committed policy or failing closed.
findings.silent_failure: The resolver exception is swallowed and the visible bubble looks like an intentionally enabled category; personal-field masking is a separate fail-closed path.
findings.regression_test: Test missing, throwing, and malformed resolver states plus explicit false and recovery; retain last-known-good or hide and emit a health diagnostic.

findings.title: Secure-field state stays stale when focus moves within one window
findings.reproduction: Focus a normal username field, then Tab or click to PASSWORD_TEXT without changing app ID or window title and type a password. process_lifecycle emits no focus callback, secure-field cache remains false, and shipped metrics defaults allow exact plaintext text/events to be flushed to SQLite; LLM filtering reads the same stale cache.
findings.root_cause: Top-level app/window identity is used as a proxy for accessible control focus, with no AT-SPI focus subscription, focus epoch, or immediate unknown state on navigation.
findings.silent_failure: No probe failed and app/title did not change, so consumers receive a valid-looking cached insecure verdict without any diagnostic.
findings.regression_test: Within one unchanged app/title, drive TEXT to PASSWORD_TEXT by Tab and click and back; require immediate unknown/fail-closed, zero pending/plaintext SQLite/log data, zero LLM request, stale-epoch rejection, and re-enable only after a fresh insecure verdict.

findings.title: Shutdown waits on external luv handles whose owners stop too late
findings.reproduction: Arm updater background checks and active file watchers with luv, then invoke tray Quit or SIGTERM. event_loop.stop closes only loop-owned handles and waits in luv.run, while updater and file-watcher owners are stopped only after run returns; referenced timer and fs_event handles therefore keep the wait alive.
findings.root_cause: External luv-handle owners are cleaned up after the event-loop wait instead of through one pre-wait shutdown transaction and complete handle registry.
findings.silent_failure: Quit ungrabs input and SIGTERM performs initial cleanup, but clean exit/flush/destroy is not reached before systemd may escalate; no-luv tests cannot reproduce it.
findings.regression_test: With real and fake luv, an armed updater timer, and active fs_event watchers, tray Quit and SIGTERM must stop/close all owned handles before the wait, return from run, execute clean exit once, and leave zero active or referenced handles.

findings.title: Hotstring priority has no collision effect and is never serialized
findings.reproduction: Use the production WebView to give the losing category of an equal-trigger collision priority 42. The live getter shows 42, but save/load omit priority, load_all never applies user overrides to mappings, and it removes exact duplicate triggers before the engine's priority sort; the winner stays unchanged live, after reload, and after restart.
findings.root_cause: Priority was added to the UI/config API without one schema spanning persistence and mapping construction, while a first-wins pre-engine dedup bypasses the only priority-aware collision arbiter.
findings.silent_failure: The live getter, bridge state push, and menu rebuild reflect the override table, so tests and UI look applied without observing the actual collision winner or a fresh reload.
findings.regression_test: Drive WebView set_priority through atomic TOML and the production mapping loader; assert the expected winner immediately, after reload, and in a fresh process for every collision tier and all shipped duplicate triggers, including clear semantics.

findings.title: Installer creates two independent startup owners
findings.reproduction: Run the standalone installer in a desktop session with a working systemd user bus. It enables and starts ergopti-hotstrings.service and also unconditionally installs an XDG autostart desktop entry with the same Exec; login can start two daemons that race EVIOCGRAB, while the losing systemd process exits 1 and can restart every three seconds.
findings.root_cause: The installer treats systemd user activation and XDG desktop autostart as cumulative setup steps instead of mutually exclusive startup-owner strategies.
findings.silent_failure: Both setup steps report success and the process that wins the grab can make typing appear functional while the other owner loops or systemd tracks the wrong process.
findings.regression_test: Install and migrate in systemd graphical, simulated XDG, and non-systemd sessions; assert exactly one startup owner, one daemon PID, one device open/grab, stable service state, no restart loop, and a working fallback.

findings.title: Production onboarding page and Linux bridge use disjoint protocols
findings.reproduction: Open onboarding through its production daemon caller and replay the shared page's real ready and finish messages. The page sends action-based messages, while the Linux bridge handles only payload.step values invented by its tests; initialization returns nil, answers are not applied or persisted, and onboarding_done is not written.
findings.root_cause: Frontend and host protocols evolved independently, and bridge-only tests model the host's private step vocabulary instead of replaying the shipped page contract.
findings.silent_failure: The page is registered and has a real opener, while tests agree with the bridge rather than the actual JavaScript, so inventories and green tests overstate runtime readiness.
findings.regression_test: Drive the real DOM protocol through the production bridge from ready to choices to finish, then start a fresh process and prove all answers are persisted and applied; require one handler per page action and an observed durable effect before any success reply.

findings.title: Hotstring editor focus never inhibits the global expansion engine
findings.reproduction: Open the production hotstring editor, focus a trigger or replacement field, and type an already-active trigger through its firing character. The page emits window_focus and the bridge sets state.editor_focused, but no production path reads that flag; the global character callback still matches and injects into the editor field.
findings.root_cause: The editor focus signal updates decorative bridge state instead of an owned, epoch-safe input-capture gate on the global engine path.
findings.silent_failure: The bridge test asserts only that the boolean changes, so it passes without typing through the real keyboard hook or observing injection.
findings.regression_test: With the real page focused, type an existing trigger and assert literal text plus zero injection, LLM, preview, and metrics; after blur assert one expansion, and prove hide, destroy, and crash cannot leave the gate stuck.

findings.title: Numeric prompt ignores host initialization and close responses
findings.reproduction: Open the custom numeric setting from its production menu caller. The page posts ready and expects receive_prompt, but defines no __hostBridgeResponse while the Linux manager sends the bridge return only through that callback; title, value, and bounds stay blank, save/cancel acknowledgements do not close the page, and a hidden reused window receives no new ready event.
findings.root_cause: The page's push API, generic Linux response API, and reusable-window lifecycle were implemented as three unconnected protocols without a request epoch.
findings.silent_failure: Unit tests inspect the Lua table returned by the bridge directly, not whether the shipped page receives or renders it or closes after completion; preset menu values remain a workaround.
findings.regression_test: Drive the real page through sequential temperature and context-length prompts and assert fresh title/value/bounds, one correct setter, acknowledged close, reopen behavior, and rejection of stale responses.

findings.title: Hotstrings settings Close button has no window owner
findings.reproduction: Click the visible Close button in the production hotstrings settings page. It sends action=close, but the bridge conditionally calls an absent state.close_webview using the unregistered key hotstrings_config instead of hotstrings_config_window; the page remains open while only the GTK title-bar X works.
findings.root_cause: Window lifecycle ownership is neither injected into bridge state nor keyed from the registered application identity.
findings.silent_failure: The bridge logs closure and returns nil without checking visibility, and tests do not observe the native window.
findings.regression_test: Click the real DOM Close button and assert one owned hide/destroy transition, is_visible=false, and a clean reopen; manifest-check every page close action against a registered app key.

findings.title: Production healthcheck opens an empty page
findings.reproduction: Open Tray > Debug > Diagnostic through its production caller. The page contains only an empty content element and passive renderHealthcheck function; it never posts ready/refresh or defines __hostBridgeResponse, while the Linux bridge builds a snapshot only in reply and the manager returns it only through that callback, so the DOM remains empty.
findings.root_cause: Renderer, request bridge, response delivery, and the Linux-specific snapshot shape were implemented independently without one page/host contract or rendered-DOM test.
findings.silent_failure: Window show succeeds, handler tests call the bridge directly, and host tests assert only assembled HTML/scripts, so every isolated layer is green without a production data flow.
findings.regression_test: Open the real production WebKit page and assert version, adapters, and Linux system fields in the DOM; refresh must reflect changed state, explicit transport errors must render, and removing either request or response wiring must fail.

findings.title: Linux release bundle and six derived formats remove every WebView application
findings.reproduction: Run the green Linux bundle build, then list build/linux/_shared/ui: only host_bridge.js, i18n.js, dom_utils.js, and apps.manifest.json exist. The build excludes ui/* and restores only those files; tarball, deb, rpm, AppImage, Flatpak, and PKGBUILD consume the truncated bundle, while webkit_host turns every missing app into non-empty error HTML that show accepts as success. The Nix flake's direct source copy is not affected by this exact exclusion.
findings.root_cause: A broad shared-UI exclusion and handwritten four-file allow-list are not derived from production openers, bridge registrations, HTML dependencies, or the page manifest.
findings.silent_failure: Build and package-layout gates verify boot paths but not UI asset closure, source-checkout execution retains the pages, and show converts a missing page into a successful registered error window.
findings.regression_test: For release tarball, deb, rpm, AppImage, Flatpak, PKGBUILD, and the separate Nix path, enumerate each production show(app), require index and referenced assets, render the expected DOM, reject app-not-found, and mutation-delete one required page or asset to make the gate fail.

findings.title: Changelog CSP blocks scripts inlined by the Linux host
findings.reproduction: Build the changelog HTML through webkit_host and load it with the production file base. Its script-src self CSP precedes application scripts that Linux converted from same-origin src tags to inline bodies without nonce/hash; makeHostBridge, _initializePage, and openOnGitHub remain undefined.
findings.root_cause: The page's CSP and the Linux host's self-contained asset-inlining strategy define mutually incompatible execution policies.
findings.silent_failure: The styled window still appears, CSP violations bypass window.onerror, and the WebKit page-error harness covers only configuration and editor pages.
findings.regression_test: Load every production-built page in WebKitGTK and assert initialization, ready signal, controls, and zero CSP violations using same-origin assets or exact nonces/hashes, never blanket unsafe-inline.

findings.title: Changelog page and Linux bridge implement three incompatible protocols
findings.reproduction: After bypassing the CSP defect, replay the page's fetch and open_url actions: the bridge knows only ready/refresh/close and open_release. Its ready result targets an absent __hostBridgeResponse callback, and its tag/notes records do not match the page's tag_name/body/html_url schema.
findings.root_cause: Action names, native response delivery, and release-record fields evolved independently without one versioned changelog contract.
findings.silent_failure: An online direct GitHub fetch after 800 ms masks native fetch failure, while the release button, native cached/offline data, and errors remain broken with only debug logging.
findings.regression_test: Drive the real DOM through ready, native cached data offline, channel change, and release open; assert one canonical schema, validated URLs, and visible network/opener failures.

findings.title: Hidden metrics WebViews continue polling the keylogger
findings.reproduction: Open either metrics dashboard, close it with the GTK title-bar X, and pump the loop for more than four seconds while instrumenting get_dashboard_payload. Its unconditional two-second JavaScript interval keeps requesting native metrics after is_visible becomes false, and reopening reuses the same context.
findings.root_cause: GTK delete-event hides and retains the WebView/JavaScript context without a visibility lifecycle that owns page timers.
findings.silent_failure: The window disappears normally and pure-Lua tests do not pump a hidden real page; the impact is continuing SQLite, aggregation, and rendering work rather than proven disclosure.
findings.regression_test: Assert zero native reads while hidden, exactly one poller after each reopen, and complete timer/WebView teardown on destroy and daemon shutdown.

findings.title: Remote CDN code inherits privileged metrics and native bridge capabilities
findings.reproduction: Replace one unpinned jsDelivr response used by a metrics page with a controlled script. With no SRI or CSP, it runs beside WebKit native handlers, can redefine __hostBridgeResponse, request/export metrics and n-grams, invoke reset/pause/edit, and exfiltrate over the unrestricted network; every registered bridge is exposed in each WebView.
findings.root_cause: Remote executable dependencies share a page context with sensitive data and globally registered native capabilities, without integrity, origin policy, or per-application bridge ownership.
findings.silent_failure: Successful HTTPS traffic looks normal, tests expect global handler registration, and no gate checks remote origins, offline completeness, asset integrity, or page-specific capabilities.
findings.regression_test: Require vendored verified dependencies, zero remote page requests, strict no-remote CSP, and one owned bridge per application; a hostile fixture must read no metric response, call no foreign bridge, and mutate no collection state.

findings.title: Personal non-ASCII aliases cannot be registered or resolved
findings.reproduction: Configure one-codepoint UTF-8 alias é for first_name and type its personal tag. Registration requires byte length one, combo resolution slices one byte at a time, and combo deletion uses byte length; a Lua fixture reports four rules instead of five, zero resolved fields, no fire, and no injection.
findings.root_cause: Three alias boundaries use Lua byte length/slicing even though the module already recognizes that user aliases are Unicode codepoints.
findings.silent_failure: The alias is skipped without rejection or log, date rules keep the module enabled, and existing concrete tests use only ASCII keys.
findings.regression_test: Test NFC é and mixed né through registration, preview, resolution, injection, and exact codepoint backspaces; reject malformed UTF-8 explicitly and mutation-fail if byte iteration returns.

findings.title: Keystrokes are logged in plaintext despite at-rest encryption
findings.reproduction: Type a sentinel printable character with metrics enabled. metrics_collector.on_keydown formats the raw character into Logger.debug, and the production keylogger always forwards accepted characters there; the default shared logger accepts DEBUG, retains it in its ring, and sends it to its sink before any SQLite encryption boundary.
findings.root_cause: The per-keystroke DEBUG message treats captured text as harmless diagnostics while the logger is a durable or observable data channel independent of the encrypted metrics store.
findings.silent_failure: At-rest encryption protects selected database columns but not logger rings or sinks, and privacy tests assert database/filter behavior rather than every log transport.
findings.regression_test: Make raw typed content unloggable by construction. In normal, private, secure, encrypted, and unencrypted modes, assert a sentinel sequence appears in neither ring buffer nor stdout, file, or journal sinks.

findings.title: Standalone upgrades freeze canonical hotstring packs at their first installed version
findings.reproduction: Install version N, then upgrade to N+1 with a changed canonical hotstring TOML. install.sh seeds canonical TOMLs into the user config only when absent, and resolve_paths lets that same-stem user copy replace the newer bundled file, so N+1 additions, corrections, and removals never load.
findings.root_cause: Complete canonical packs are seeded as user overrides without version, hash, or provenance, yet same-stem user files have unconditional precedence over bundled packs.
findings.silent_failure: The installer correctly reports configuration preservation and both files parse; source and fresh-install tests do not exercise a versioned upgrade or distinguish an intact seed from a user modification.
findings.regression_test: Test N to N+1 with an intact seeded pack receiving additions, corrections, and removals, a modified pack retained as a deliberate override, and a fresh process resolving the expected source.

findings.title: Clipboard fallback destroys existing content after a read failure
findings.reproduction: Seed a logical clipboard with COPIED-SECRET, make the X11 or Wayland read command fail, and keep clipboard writes and uinput paste events successful. The shell adapter converts the failure to an empty string, paste_text treats it as its snapshot, restores empty content, and returns true.
findings.root_cause: Clipboard read uses one untyped string result, so an operational read failure is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty clipboard and the fallback transaction begins without a valid snapshot.
findings.silent_failure: Existing fakes model only readable text and adapter conformance checks the happy path; all write and injection steps can succeed while the previous clipboard content is silently lost.
findings.regression_test: Test a real empty clipboard separately from failed X11 and Wayland reads. On failure require zero writes and paste events, preserved original clipboard content, and false propagated to the injector transaction.

findings.title: Kanata configuration writes can destroy the last good file yet report success
findings.reproduction: Inject a Kanata config file whose write returns disk full and whose close returns I/O error. write_kbd opens the final file with w, ignores both failures, logs success, and returns true; restart can then stop Kanata and attempt to start it with an empty or partial config.
findings.root_cause: The remap manager bypasses Storage with a destructive direct write and publishes success without checking write, flush, close, or an atomic replacement.
findings.silent_failure: Meta tests conditionally skip assertions when the operation or file handle is unavailable, so failure paths do not inspect prior content, return value, lifecycle, or success logging.
findings.regression_test: Fault open, short write, flush, close, and rename independently. Require false, byte-identical prior config, no Kanata stop or start, and no success log; on success verify exact content after atomic replacement.

findings.title: Kanata stop failure is reported as success and loses process ownership
findings.reproduction: Hold an owned Kanata PID, make its TERM fail while kill -0 confirms it remains alive, then restart. stop ignores the failed kill, clears ownership, and restart reports success although the old process still runs with the old configuration.
findings.root_cause: stop has no checked result contract and clears its owned PID before confirming termination, so restart can continue from a false lifecycle state.
findings.silent_failure: Tests cover stop without a process and foreign-process protection but do not simulate a failed stop of a process owned by the manager.
findings.regression_test: Simulate failed TERM and stubborn owned process; require false, retained ownership, no stopped or restarted success log, and no new launch. Cover bounded delayed successful termination separately.

findings.title: A recycled Kanata PID can terminate an unrelated user process
findings.reproduction: Start fake Kanata with PID N, let it exit, reuse N for an unrelated fake editor, then call is_running and stop. Bare kill -0 treats the editor as owned Kanata and stop signals it.
findings.root_cause: The remap manager stores only a numeric PID with no child handle, exit watcher, start time, or executable identity, so kernel PID reuse is indistinguishable from the original process.
findings.silent_failure: Foreign-instance tests start with no owned PID and lifecycle tests do not recycle a PID after a formerly owned child exits.
findings.regression_test: Reuse an exited owned PID for another process and require no ownership, no signal, survivor intact, no stopped log, and inactive Kanata state; test handle or verified identity fallback separately.
